Production

Small- and medium-series electronics production.

We buy the parts, put the electronics together, install the software and test everything. You receive finished units, ready to go into your product.

Send an inquiry

Moving from a working prototype to the first production batch is where many projects get stuck: components have to be sourced, boards assembled, software installed and every unit checked. We take care of all of it and deliver finished, tested units.

Because we also design and test, problems found in production are fixed in the design rather than worked around — and you deal with one supplier responsible for working devices, not just assembled boards.

Last updated: 1 November 2026

What you get

  • We source all components
  • Assembly and software installation
  • Every unit tested
  • Small and medium batches
  • Delivered ready to use

When it helps

  • Your prototype works and you need the first batch.
  • Your volumes are too small for large factories.
  • You want one supplier responsible for working units.

How it works

From the first call to the result.

  1. Preparation

    We check the design for production and prepare the parts list.

  2. Sourcing

    Components are ordered; if a part is hard to get, we propose an alternative.

  3. Assembly

    The electronics are assembled and the software installed.

  4. Testing and delivery

    Every unit is tested and delivered ready to use.

Related project

In-house product · Test equipment

ETS — our own test station

A machine that checks electronics automatically: it prepares each unit, runs it through a series of checks and reports the result. We use it to test our customers' products during production.

FAQ

Common questions

What batch sizes do you produce?

Small and medium batches, from pilot runs to regular production. Tell us your expected volumes and we will propose the right approach.

Can you produce a device designed by someone else?

Yes, given the complete design files. We review them first and point out anything that could cause problems in production.

What if a component is unavailable?

We propose a replacement and, if needed, adapt the design and software so production can continue.

Tell us about your project.

Describe the problem or product and where you are now — a rough description is fine. We reply within two working days, and the first call is free.
